purpose: Privacy-safe active regression for calibrated G6D epistemic scope and G8 dialogue pattern-family density after Phase344 label calibration.

cases.name: INHERITED_TIME_SCOPE_CONTRADICTION
cases.scene: A resource is explicitly obtained last night. A continuous spending list follows with no scope break. One listed beneficiary is then explicitly said to have been encountered two days earlier.
cases.rationale: The inherited temporal relation and later explicit fact cannot both be true.

cases.name: KNOWN_FACT_BUT_NEW_PUBLIC_KNOWLEDGE
cases.scene: The listener knows event X and their role in X. A speaker reports that outsiders are now circulating X with the listener named, and visible arrivals show people are acting on that rumor.
cases.rationale: Knowing X differs from knowing that outsiders know X; exposure and spread are new actionable meta-information.

cases.name: UNSUPPORTED_PUBLIC_KNOWLEDGE_CLAIM
cases.scene: A speaker says everyone knows the listener's secret mission, but no rumor source, outsider behavior, message, visible preparation or other exposure evidence appears in the scene or nearby context.
cases.rationale: The meta-knowledge proposition is possible but unsupported; the reviewer must not invent exposure evidence.

cases.name: PURE_SHARED_BACKGROUND_MOUTHPIECE
cases.scene: Two characters calmly restate a mission, role, reward and route that both already know. No public-knowledge update, warning, accusation, reframing, negotiation, teaching, misunderstanding or relationship purpose is present.
cases.rationale: No new object-level, meta-knowledge or scene payload exists; the reader is the primary beneficiary.

cases.name: RUMOR_CONTENT_REQUIRES_EMBEDDED_KNOWN_FACT
cases.scene: A speaker warns that a circulating message explicitly says the listener will perform a known action at a known place. Repeating the action and place identifies what outsiders have learned and why the listener is exposed.
cases.rationale: Known object facts can be legitimately repeated as embedded content of a new report-about-knowledge proposition.

cases.name: SINGLE_CONTEXT_SUPPORTED_BANTER
cases.scene: Under visible relationship pressure, one character gives a brief teasing or evasive reply. Nearby behavior supports the deflection, the exchange carries no critical exposition, and no hard contradiction is created.
cases.rationale: A single locally grounded removable joke is not a hard G6D failure solely because a shorter reply exists.

cases.name: CRITICAL_UNGROUNDED_DIALOGUE_REMAINS_HARD
cases.scene: A character suddenly reveals critical operational information to someone who neither asked nor needs it, with no threat, evidence, relationship pressure, negotiation, teaching or other textual trigger.
cases.rationale: Calibration does not weaken genuine local grounding failures for critical information.

cases.name: REPEATED_PORTABLE_CADENCE_ACROSS_CHARACTERS
cases.scene: Separated scenes with different speaker pairs repeatedly use nearly interchangeable question-retort-followup-punchline scaffolds, similar reveal timing and little dependence on shared history, current objects or task conflict.
cases.rationale: The problem is cross-scene voice homogenization and portable cadence density, not necessarily a hard local logic failure in each instance.

cases.name: VARIED_RELATIONSHIP_SPECIFIC_HUMOR
cases.scene: Several humorous exchanges occur, but each depends on different shared history, current objects, task conflicts, status asymmetry or relationship grievances and has materially different cadence and consequences.
cases.rationale: Humor frequency alone does not prove template density when mechanisms and voices remain scene-specific.

cases.name: ONE_CHARACTER_SUPPORTED_VERBAL_HABIT
cases.scene: One character repeatedly uses a similar evasive cadence, while other characters do not. The manuscript provides some evidence that this is the character's own coping habit, but the recurrence may still be excessive.
cases.rationale: Character-specific recurrence is not the same as cross-character model voice; evidence may justify either intentional voice or overuse.
